questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Figure out your commute to the university prior to going. It may become expensive and inflexible if you are required to go by public transport, Uber or a like every day.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *

questions.answer: I got into all (5) classes I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do a proper due diligence prior to arrival. Read up on the professors teaching the courses - enjoy you are an exchange student and it does not really matter whether it is a tough course grade wise, as your visit is about learning.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level does not differ much from Copenhagen. A lot more homework / preparation is required.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Many professors use the socratic method of teaching, whereas UCPH is, in my opinion, built on one-way communication not offering a lot of in-class analysis, due to the UCPH not requiring students to proper prepare for classes / not punishing those, who do not.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Business Associations w. Professor Raskin.
2. Corporate Finance w. Professor De Fontaney
3. Distinctive Aspects of US Law w. professor Metzloff
4. U.S. Legal Analysis, Research, and Writing for International Students w. professor Stuart.
5. Business & Economics of a Law Firm w. professor Elvin.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 3 & 4 are essential to a proper U.S. legal education experience. Rest are based on personal interest.

questions.answer: Making sure to make close friends with the LLM class.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get into the sports / non-curricular activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Duke has a great academic programme - however, it is located in a boring city.
Consider reaching out to fellow students prior to going to arrange housing. Faculty may be supportive in this endeavour.
Pick classes based on interest and the professor - as an exchange student your grades are not as important, so you should challenge yourself within your area of interest.
